semantic_correction.stem: A client is planning international travel. Which nursing recommendation best reflects current CDC pre-travel guidance?

options.A: Base the plan on the traveler’s health history, immunization status, itinerary, trip duration, and planned activities, then tailor vaccines and exposure precautions.
options.B: Use the destination as the main factor; travelers going to the same country generally need the same vaccine and prevention plan regardless of health history or activities.
options.C: Concentrate on destination vaccines; food, water, vector, and activity-related precautions can wait until the traveler develops symptoms during the trip.
options.D: Focus on medical history and routine vaccines; itinerary details and planned activities add little to pre-travel risk assessment when the traveler is otherwise healthy.

semantic_correction.rationale: A is correct. The CDC Yellow Book 2026 states that an effective pre-travel consultation uses the traveler’s health background together with itinerary, trip duration, travel purpose, and planned activities to assess risk and individualize prevention. Vaccine recommendations depend on destination and itinerary, and counseling can also address food- and water-borne infection, vector-borne disease, and other likely exposures. B is incorrect because travelers to the same country can require different recommendations based on personal health and trip details. C is incorrect because exposure-prevention counseling is a core preventive component of the consultation before travel. D is incorrect because itinerary and planned activities are explicit parts of CDC’s individual risk assessment even when the traveler is otherwise healthy.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Individualize pre-travel counseling using both the traveler’s medical and immunization history and the specific itinerary, duration, purpose, and planned activities, then provide destination-relevant vaccination and exposure-prevention teaching.

semantic_correction.source_locator: The Pre-Travel Consultation — Introduction: effective consultations require attention to the traveler’s health background and incorporate itinerary, trip duration, travel purpose, and planned activities. Assess individual risk: personal health background, immunization history, trip itinerary/timing/reason/style/activities, and infectious-disease status at destination. Manage risk — Vaccinations: destination, purpose, season, duration, and specific itinerary inform vaccine need. Personalized advice includes likely exposures such as foodborne/waterborne and vector-borne disease. Food and Water Precautions for Travelers — Introduction: contaminated food and water are infectious risks and travelers should receive prevention counseling.
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: CDC recommends individualized pre-travel risk assessment based on the traveler’s health background and trip details, with vaccination and other prevention counseling tailored to the destination, itinerary, activities, and likely exposures.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item tests individualized pre-travel risk assessment with one clearly best answer, clinically plausible distractors, and no answer-length or absolute-word cue.

option_audit.A: Correct. It includes the traveler characteristics and trip-specific factors CDC explicitly uses to individualize risk assessment, vaccination, and exposure prevention.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Destination matters, but CDC also requires individual health background, immunization history, itinerary, duration, purpose, travel style, and activities; same-country travelers can need different plans.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Food, water, vector, and activity-related risks are addressed preventively during the pre-travel consultation rather than deferred until illness occurs.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. CDC explicitly includes itinerary and planned activities in the pre-travel risk assessment even for otherwise healthy travelers.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A is the only option that incorporates both traveler-specific and itinerary-specific risk assessment and then tailors preventive interventions; B, C, and D each omit CDC-defined core elements.
cueing_check: The choices are closely balanced in length (A 165, B 171, C 153, D 168 characters), use parallel counseling-plan language, and contain no unique absolute wording or formatting that identifies A.
